title: mini-retro: sample friction + SDK migration notes
content:
Attendees: Asha, Ethan, Maya, Owen, Lena (15m)

Context: quick mini-retrospective after two sprints of the SDK migration pilot + sample kit rollout. We surfaced recurring friction points developers hit when switching between v1 -> v2 SDK and when running quickstarts locally versus CI. Goal: capture small, high-impact fixes we can ship in the next week and things that need design/PM.

Summary (TL;DR):
- Several sample templates still import legacy helper functions (auth & env); causes confusion for new users. Two high-priority fixes: update templates and add local env validation in quickstart CLI.
- Inconsistent telemetry labels across SDK and samples (metrics/route names). Leads to noisy dashboards and some missing telemetry for quickstarts. Need a small mapping/compat shim and a follow-up to standardize naming.
- CI flakiness on mac M1 CI runners due to wheel/conda mismatch for a binary dep in samples. Short term: pin a platform-specific wheel in CI matrix; long term: vendor-build or switch to pure-python fallback.
- Docs: quickstart step that asks for API key is buried in a parent README and not shown in the single-page quickstart. Add a short callout and checkbox early in the quickstart.

Notes / Observations:
- Migration pain point A (imports): sample templates under samples/python/quickstarts still reference redwood_sdk.helpers.get_env() which moved to redwood_infra.env.get. New users copy-paste and hit ImportError. (Related PR: samples PR #542)
- Migration pain point B (auth): example code uses an implicit `REDWOOD_API_KEY` lookup; quickstart CLI attempts to be helpful but exits with a non-descriptive error code. Owen reproduced in-person: error logs showed KeyError with no guidance.
- Telemetry: SDK v2 emits metric name `dx.sdk.init.start` while sample harness emits `devexp.sdk.start`. Dashboards expect `dx.sdk.*` so sample events get dropped from the quickstarts funnel.
- CI: mac runner logs show `error: cannot find _native_ext` when building wheel for dependency `fastparse_c`. This only appears on mac-arm64 matrix entries. Ethan suggests trying wheel-for-arch pinned build cache.
- UX: Quickstart page length mismatch: website quickstart (single page) is trimmed and omits the env+auth section which is present in the repo README -> onboarding fails for first-time users.

Decisions made (quick):
- Patch-level changes (docs + templates + CLI messages) approved to ship in patch release this week. Owner: Asha. Target: patch cut 2026-11-24.
- Telemetry shim: add a small adapter in samples harness that maps `devexp.*` -> `dx.*` for the next 2 releases; schedule a follow-up to standardize all naming across SDK + samples. Owner: Maya. Target: 2026-12-08 for shim, 2026-12-22 for standardization RFC.
- CI pin: add mac-arm64 pinned wheel for `fastparse_c` in samples CI matrix and add a note in infra tickets. Owner: Ethan. Target: 2026-11-23.

Action items (who / what / due):
- Asha: update python quickstart templates to import new helper paths, add a one-liner at the top calling out "set REDWOOD_API_KEY or run `rwd login`"; update sample README and single-page quickstart snippet. (due 2026-11-24)
- Maya: implement telemetry shim in samples harness + unit tests; open RFC issue for naming standardization. Include mapping table in PR. (shim due 2026-12-08; RFC issue due 2026-11-26)
- Ethan: CI change to pin wheel and add fallback build step for mac-arm64; coordinate with infra to cache wheel artifacts. (due 2026-11-23)
- Owen: improve quickstart CLI UX—catch KeyError on missing env and print explicit next steps & link to docs. Small UX copy provided below. (due 2026-11-24)
- Lena: write a small 1-paragraph release note blurb for the SDK patch + samples fixes; coordinate with docs for next website push. (due 2026-11-25)

Quick UX copy (for Owen to use):
- On missing API key: "No API key found. Set REDWOOD_API_KEY in your environment or run `rwd login` to authenticate. See quickstart steps: <link>."
- On import error: "This quickstart uses the v2 SDK. Run `pip install redwood-sdk==2.*` or follow the migration guide: <link>."

Open questions / follow-ups:
- Do we want the telemetry shim to live in samples or in a small helper package shared by SDK and samples? (tradeoff: faster shipping vs discoverability). Maya to propose in RFC.
- Should quickstart CI include a smoke-run step that actually runs the onboarding flow (fast, headless) to catch missing env/instructions in the single-page quickstart? Strong +1 from team; need time estimate.
- Should we add a migration lint that flags legacy import paths in PRs touching samples? Could be a quick rule in the repo CI. Owen to prototype.

Related links and refs:
- GH: sdk PR 1287 (v2 auth surfaces) — https://github.com/redwood-inference/sdk/pull/1287
- GH: samples PR 542 (quickstart fixes) — https://github.com/redwood-inference/samples/pull/542
- Jira: RINF-4871 — "Quickstarts: missing env guidance causes onboarding failures"
- Confluence: Sample Kit Migration Plan — confluence.redwood.ai/display/DX/Sample+Kit+Migration+Plan

Misc notes / voice-of-customer snippets (copied from support slack):
- "I followed the quickstart and then hit ImportError: cannot import name 'get_env' — spent 30 mins."
- "The one-page quickstart on the website doesn't mention authentication — surprised why it fails in step 2." 

Next check-in: brief async update in #devexp on 2026-11-23 with PR links; follow-up sync if blockers remain (2026-11-24 30m).
